note: Seeded overlap CANDIDATES only. A pair here is a starting point for detection, never a verdict: verdicts live in the committed store (docs/native-surfaces/records.json by default) and are human-gated. Adding a pair here proposes a row; it does not create one.

pairs.why: Both review a diff or a PR for correctness findings; the names collide outright.
Both clean up changed code without changing behavior.
Same cleanup job at batch scale across many files.
Both produce a security-focused review of a change; the extraction reports the native side under plugin_backed, not builtin_commands.
Both launch the project's app to see a change actually working.
Both look at the health of a Claude Code installation.
Both diagnose a slow or unhealthy install; doctor also offers to fix.
doctor's checkup covers unused extensions and skill visibility as one pass of a broader health check; the audit asks the whole-fleet visibility question.
Both ask which loaded skills go unused and what each costs; the built-in is a one-shot report that excludes bundled skills, the audit is the fleet-wide visibility question.
Both assemble an operator morning view. Session-provided, so it is observation-only: absent from the vendored binary's bundled set.
clean-stop, handoff, and retro suggest the built-in /export at session-end moments; the command is the only stable conversation-export surface and the skills reference it by name.
Both can answer 'show me this visually'; the first-party plugin's interactive explorer with a prompt round-trip overlaps visualize's rich-page medium.
Both build a browser page with switchable controls; explore-directions varies your project's own UI while a playground explores an arbitrary parameter space.
visualize already routes hand-tweakable layouts to the bundled design canvas; the live integration deserves a recorded verdict.
explore-directions offers the design-canvas Artifact as one of its mockup surfaces; same live integration, sibling component.

Both answer 'where does this session stand'; recap summarizes the conversation, orient reads durable state the conversation never saw. The two share almost no vocabulary, so discovery scores the pair low.
Both hand the current work to a background agent that carries the conversation forward.
Both send an agent off with the session's context; subtask returns its result here, continue-in-background detaches it.
Both plan a large change and fan it out to worker agents; the name tokens never meet, so discovery misses the pair.
Both explain where a session's tokens and cost went.
Both attribute context consumption to what caused it; the audit measures the startup payload, explain-usage the whole session.
Both work from the permission rules in effect; the native skill writes an allowlist from observed usage, the audit reports what is in effect and what auto mode drops.
The design-sync family (sync, consent, revoke, login) is registered in the binary near the canvas skill visualize gates; recorded to rule on, not to integrate.

The built-in agents-md plugin loads AGENTS.md as project instructions where no CLAUDE.md exists; migrate moves a repository's instructions into AGENTS.md and decides whether its CLAUDE.md shim is still needed.

The built-in claude-test plugin runs plain-language specs against a local dev server in a headless browser and reports PASS/FAIL with screenshots; run-e2e drives end-to-end tests of the running app. Gated off by tengu_mellow_hollerith (default false) as of 2.1.287.
claude-test drives a fenced headless browser through a bundled playwright-mcp; the playwright skill drives the same browser automation directly.

The built-in you-should-know mod has a side agent watch longer tasks and raise a note about what the person may not know; blindspot surfaces what the person has not considered. Off by default (defaultEnabled false, tengu_jolly_dewdrop default false) as of 2.1.287.

The built-in responsive-mode mod adds a system-prompt section that has Claude reply in a sentence first and bans flattery, corporate vocabulary and wrap-ups; be-concise tightens replies the same way. Off by default (defaultEnabled false, tengu_quiet_ember default false) as of 2.1.287.

The built-in mermaid mod draws mermaid flowcharts and sequence diagrams in replies as box-drawing text in the terminal; visualize emits Mermaid diagrams. Gated off by tengu_mermaid_mod (default false) as of 2.1.287.
